patch.value: Agent-environment programme: pm as the task substrate, verifier, and trajectory source for RL training, evaluation, benchmarking and simulation workflows

Programme-level container, filed 2026-07-31 because the capability already exists in pieces and has no single owner. Duplicate check: searched RL, environment, episode, trajectory, benchmark, corpus generator and deterministic reset lineages; every constituent item was found and none is duplicated here. This epic organizes them and names what is missing between them; it does not restate their scope and does not re-parent them, since each is correctly parented by the capability it modifies.

Why a programme rather than another capability epic. The existing eighteen epics partition the product by subsystem - storage, graph, MCP, scale, schema. This work cuts across four of them at once and is coherent only when read end to end. Today its constituent items are parented in four different places: pm-nfrhf0 (the environment-author story) and pm-li2fj5 (episode substrate) under pm-8jdc schema and config; pm-qd6gvf (trajectory projection) under pm-o2kc storage and history; pm-8bgeye (attested context reads) and pm-tch9cs (fleet-amortized assembly) under pm-9rxu scale-out. Nothing reads them as one deliverable, so no one owns the seams between them. This follows the pattern already established by pm-wjfa, pm-92if and pm-n7rr, which are cross-cutting programmes rather than subsystems.

What already exists and is shipped, so the programme starts from a real base rather than a blank one. pm-rbcvt2 delivered reproducible workspace instances with seeded identifiers, an injectable clock and byte-identical construction, which is the reset primitive any environment needs. pm-mi2x delivered the scale benchmark harness with synthetic 10k, 100k and 1M item generators plus latency, memory and token baselines. pm-vv2lti corrected those fixtures so population shape varies rather than only size. The immutable history stream, hash-chained and restorable to any version, is the trajectory source. Together these are most of a usable environment substrate; what is missing is the contract that presents them as one.

The four seams this epic owns, none of which belongs to a single constituent item.

First, episode identity across surfaces and processes. An episode spans several pm invocations, some through the CLI and some through MCP, and the only per-session key today is agent_instance. pm-1zhfls proves that key is already unreliable for provenance because one session records different dimensions depending on surface, and pm-rbg1qo shows no role or topic has ever been recorded. Without a stable, labelled episode key, trajectory projection cannot group and fleet analytics cannot aggregate. This is the programme's binding prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.

Second, the verdict contract. pm-li2fj5 composes a computed verdict into the episode unit. What is undefined is the boundary between a verdict pm computes from recorded state - which is auditable, reproducible and the whole point - and a reward an environment author computes outside pm. Getting that boundary wrong in either direction is costly: too narrow and every author reimplements state inspection, too wide and pm acquires opinions about reward shaping that belong to the training loop.

Third, the observation contract. pm-8bgeye makes an assembly attestable and pm-tch9cs shares assemblies across a fleet. An environment needs a bounded observation whose token cost is declared before the call, so a training run can budget. That is the same requirement as pm-5t33or's contract-declared output budgets, viewed from the environment side, and the two should resolve to one mechanism rather than two.

Fourth, non-PM domains. pm-t4d7nz requires non-PM systems to be buildable on SDK primitives alone. An RL environment is the most demanding such system, because it needs reset, step, observe and score with reproducibility guarantees, and it therefore functions as the acceptance test for that milestone. pm-z5pmf8 blocks it directly: while the SDK's lifecycle surface re-exports CLI command modules, an environment author cannot compose a step from primitives without depending on the CLI layer.

Deliberately out of scope: any opinion about model training, reward shaping, or a specific RL framework. pm supplies substrate - reproducible state, bounded observation, recorded trajectory, computed verdict - and stops there.

An environment author can run a complete episode - reset, step, observe, score - through public SDK primitives alone, with no import from src/cli and no shelling out, demonstrated by a worked example under docs/examples; A stable episode identity spans every surface and process an episode touches, is recorded in the immutable stream, and groups a trajectory correctly when a session mixes CLI and MCP calls; The boundary between a pm-computed verdict and an author-computed reward is stated as a contract, with pm's side reproducible from recorded state and independently checkable; Observation cost is declared before the call and honoured, so a training loop can budget tokens per step without measuring empirically; The programme's own scale claim is proved on a generated corpus at the 100k and 1M points using the existing harness, reporting per-step latency and observation size rather than only assembly latency; Reproducibility is proved end to end: the same episode specification and seed produce byte-identical workspace state and an identical verdict across runs and across platforms; Every constituent item retains its capability parent and carries a typed edge to this epic, so the programme is traversable without moving ownership

value.text: Long-horizon agent-environment plan 2026-08-01: pm supplies a framework-neutral substrate, not a training framework. Phase A stabilizes episode identity, deterministic reset, action and observation schemas, verdict predicates, trajectory projection, and point-in-time replay. Phase B adds bounded observation costs, attestation, dataset export, seeded fault and concurrency simulation, and reproducibility across OS and process boundaries. Phase C scales episodes across 100k and 1M-item corpora and thousand-agent fleets with resumable streams, content-addressed shared observations, privacy-safe provenance, and contamination controls. Phase D publishes environment and benchmark authoring kits, offline evaluation adapters, sim-to-real validation hooks, and domain packs. Every phase stays SDK-only, versioned, replayable, and auditable; reward shaping, model policy, and framework-specific orchestration remain external.

author: harness:codex
message: Release after ecosystem roadmap organization and verification
